summary: Independent fresh-context re-review of the fully re-executed runner_direct evidence chain. Reviewer independence note: the reviewer was a separate subagent with fresh context, but its own session id is not self-observable, so the lifecycle records the dispatching session rather than the reviewer's; reviewer_identity is therefore left unasserted rather than claimed. Findings: the round-3 disclosure defects are resolved, no hand-edited observation prose survives, all four surface_hash values were independently recomputed and match byte-for-byte, and the substantive claims were verified against the named files (typecheck glob widening, lint 70/70, the 17 deleted files matching REMOVED_VACUOUS_FILES exactly, the four integration scenarios, and the AC-3/AC-4 suites rerun 7/7). The head split with unit at 55131e55 and the other three at bff8fe0a is benign under content_surface mode because 55131e55 touches only .vibepro/config.json and two docs/management/decisions files. Two medium defects remain, both in content binding rather than in claim truth.

findings.detail: The unit record places test/execution-state.test.js next to the AC-3 and AC-4 markers and binds it in content_binding.surface_files, but that file carries neither claim: zero hits for bypassed, hasExplicitDelivery and deriveCompletedPhases, and its only completed_phases includes agent_review assertion at line 1382 asserts false. The files that do carry the claims, test/e2e/story-vibepro-execution-judgment-status-integrity-main.test.js line 69 and test/e2e/story-vibepro-managed-worktree-gate-main.test.js line 110, are unbound, so emptying either would leave the evidence reported current. Demonstrated harm: a round-2 gate_evidence review wrote the false statement that execution-state.test.js asserts the agent_review derivation, caused by this adjacency.

All four e2e targets use the AC-N colon path form, so normalizeSurfacePath at src/content-binding.js line 119 takes the leading whitespace-delimited token as the path and drops it. missing_files records AC-1, AC-2, AC-5, AC-6 and the lane's real bound surface is scripts/lint-e2e-product-execution.mjs alone; neither the acceptance spec nor scripts/run-e2e-ts-specs.mjs is bound. The unit lane already demonstrates the workaround of listing bare paths alongside markers.

unit.log retains only the last 262144 of 559174 bytes, honestly disclosed as log_truncated true. Neither AC-3 nor AC-4 test name survives in the retained log, so the unit lane's own artifact cannot confirm the two markers it carries; the substance is confirmable from e2e.log lines 148-149 and by rerunning the two files.

No prior version of verification-evidence.json exists to diff, since .vibepro is git-excluded, this Story has no audit-artifacts directory, and the .vibepro-store copy is identical to the live file. The conclusion that every traceable removal was the withdrawal of a claim a prior round found untrue, and that no true load-bearing claim was dropped, rests on the six gate_evidence results in the review history rather than on a byte diff.

inspection.summary: Recomputed all four content_binding surface_hash values independently and confirmed byte-for-byte match; read the named source and test files to check each target and scenario claim against what its command executes; reran the two AC-3/AC-4 test files (7/7 pass) and the e2e product-execution lint (70/70); ran npm run typecheck; traced normalizeSurfacePath to explain the dropped AC-N targets; and reconstructed prior evidence claims from the six historical gate_evidence results to test for silently dropped coverage.

judgment_delta: Established that the re-executed chain is truthful in its claims and free of the round-3 disclosure defects, and separately that two of the four lanes bind the wrong files, so a change to the code the AC-3, AC-4 and e2e acceptance claims depend on would not stale the evidence that asserts them.
